dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Hello! Would you like to practice some music?

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: (A sign-in board identical in style to the ones in the city.)

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: There you are, little one. I knew I'd find you here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Miko.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...That's all you have to say? After all this time apart? How devastating.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: To think of all the times that I've sat down beneath the Sacred Sakura, praying for your wellbeing on your travels...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: But I think I understand. Another wise and beautiful soul has stolen your heart, haven't they? I'm sure you cast aside the omamori I gave you long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Alas, I am but another fleeting passerby on your journey... Oh, woe is me...

choices.text: I see you haven't lost your sense of humor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You can always count on Miko to tease {NICKNAME} relentlessly.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: #Well, it's not my fault that {M#he's}{F#she's} the most appealing little Fortune Slip in the world. If I didn't indulge my curiosity by taking a peek inside, goodness knows how I'd sleep at night.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Though I must say, another interesting Fortune Slip caught my attention recently. I believe you've heard of it too.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: This "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"... Something to do with a dog, apparently.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: My first thought was... I wonder if it could be the Boss of Komore Teahouse, Taroumaru.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Taroumaru!? Yeah, he might actually have what it takes! Hmm, you think he was the one rescuing animals during the war?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Sounds likely, doesn't it? Boss of a teahouse by day, changes outfit after work, then runs to a warzone to save lives... And what a fascinating character it would make for a light novel.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But the question is... Do we think he was only saving animals?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you saying you know something?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'm just speculating, little one. You know how much I like to let my imagination run wild.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I look forward to opening up this Fortune Slip. Who knows what might be written inside?

choices.text: Nonsense, how could I ever forget the amazing Yae Miko!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shikanoin Heizou's Message

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: Itto, I've received your invitation letter. Everyone's happy for you.

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: We believe that you've got a good head for event planning. If you work a little harder, I'm sure you'll stop having to report to us all the time.

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: So please, take these Lavender Melons with compliments from the Police Station.

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: Oh, yes. Madam Kujou Sara also wishes us to pass this message along on her behalf: "The Tenryou Commission is watching you. Do not forget that."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Message from "TCG Buddy Ayato"

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: I was delighted to hear that you were holding another festival, Itto. As such, I have commissioned a set of audio equipment as a congratulatory gift.

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: Also, I have recently heard the children of Hanamizaka saying, "Ayato of the South, Itto of the North." Could you enlighten me as to what that means?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thoma's Message

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: Hey, Itto, this is your second time organizing this sort of musical event, right? Haha, didn't think you'd move the stage to Watatsumi Island — opposite Sangonomiya Shrine, no less. Very cool!

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: I asked our Clan Head, and it was agreed that we dispatch a team from Komore Teahouse to help liven up the atmosphere.

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: They'll provide tourists with free tea. What do you think? Pretty sweet, eh?

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it, you're welcome. I'm happy as long as you are!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yoimiya's Message

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry, my bad! I actually received your letter quite a while ago, but choosing the fireworks proved kinda tricky, and I wasn't familiar with the route, so there were some delays.

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: That said, when I got here, I thought everything was going great! The atmosphere's electric, the scenery's beautiful... Ah, I'm going to have a good, long look around.

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: I hope the fireworks will fit in well with your gang's rock 'n' roll festival!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Message from "Ramen Buddy"

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: Well, well, Sir Arataki, I didn't think you'd remember little old me, your ramen buddy. I've since spent many nights considering how I might express my thanks.

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: See that standing sign over there? Yes, that's right, it's your beloved Ms. Hina. It was a last-minute decision, and I spent quite a hefty sum on this one.

dialogues.speaker: "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"
dialogues.text: You wouldn't disappoint me by not placing it in the most conspicuous of locations, such that Ms. Hina might be put on full display to the people of Watatsumi Island in all her glory, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave

dialogues.speaker: Observe Sign-In Board
dialogues.text: (A sign-in board identical in style to the ones in the city.)

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: (This letter is elegantly written, and has been signed "Shikanoin Heizou.")

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Read the letter

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: I asked some Ritou residents, but none of them have heard of that which you call "ninken" on the battlefield.

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: The sheer lack of information quite surpassed my expectations. This is quite strange, even for information that has not yet spread widely.

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: I will continue searching for clues.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Read the second letter

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: I tried a different approach today, which unexpectedly yielded some relevant information.

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: During the war, the International Trade Association had an organization registered with it that specialized in pet treatment and trade known as the "Puppy Union."

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Its symbol just happens to be a dog wearing a bamboo hat. Not that this proves anything alone, but I found two other suspicious things:

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: 1. After the war, the Puppy Union very quickly canceled its registration.

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: 2. The Puppy Union's event funding went through at least six layers of transfers, quite suspicious...

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: I will continue investigating.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Read the third letter

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Well, well, wasn't this quite the day?

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: I tried to investigate the people who had dealings with this Puppy Union as much as I could, and I found two main, hidden sources of funding.

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: One is the Foreign Trade Association. In fact, the Union could be considered a subsidiary of the former.

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: You may not be aware of the particulars regarding said Union, but they are closely connected to Sangonomiya.

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: The second source is more interesting still. You'd never guess, but it's Komore Teahouse, and of course... the Yashiro Commission isn't far behind the curtain.

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: A fascinating turn of events, no? Sangonomiya and the Yashiro Commission... I wonder what your little secret is?

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: I have my guesses, but I'll need more evidence to prove it — details of deals regarding pets.

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: We should have records of such things at the Police Station. I'll get in touch with Yoriki Owada.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave

dialogues.speaker: Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: (This letter is elegantly written, and has been signed "Shikanoin Heizou.")

response.speaker: Strange Daruma
response.text: ...Grow...

response.speaker: Strange Daruma
response.text: ...Can't... grow... taller...

response.speaker: Strange Daruma
response.text: ...Mmmm...

dialogues.speaker: Komore Teahouse Signboard
dialogues.text: Free tea breaks, courtesy of Komore Teahouse. Enjoy to your heart's content!

dialogues.speaker: Komore Teahouse Signboard
dialogues.text: Please do not touch the Daruma. It is not a staff member.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}. Thanks again for all of your help. Everything went perfectly! I think I'm gonna stay here for a while, and just enjoy the scenery.

choices.text: I'd like to try playing another song.

response.speaker: Dvorak
response.text: Sure, no problem. Be my guest.

response.speaker: Dvorak
response.text: Sure thing. Like I said, I'll be here for a while, so you know where to find me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll have a go.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Great. Before you get started, you'll want to calibrate your instrument — everyone's playing style is slightly different. Lemme help you with that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to decorate the venue.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Oh, really? You've got the things from the list? Great, I'll take those. Thanks so much!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not right now. Maybe later.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: No problem. I'll be here if you need me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll have a go.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Great! I've been looking forward to hearing you play.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>I'd like to decorate the venue.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Oh, really? You've got the things from the list? Great, I'll take those. Thanks so much!

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! This "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness" you recommended really is awesome. I've been inspired!

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Now have a taste of the food I made specifically for the event!

dialogues.speaker: Langqing
dialogues.text: #Is that you, {NICKNAME}? Oh my! I've heard so much about you from Fangfang.

choices.text: You have me at a disadvantage, sir.

response.speaker: Langqing
response.text: Ah, right! I forgot to introduce myself. I'm Langqing. Fangfang is Wanwen Bookhouse's Jifang. She's my wife, you see. She was the one who told me about this event.

response.speaker: Langqing
response.text: I don't know much about rock 'n' roll, but Fangfang says that we should support the latest cultural trends, so here I am.

response.speaker: Langqing
response.text: I brought some free cultural products as well. They got snapped up in a heartbeat! Ah, if only I'd known, I'd have brought more.

response.speaker: Langqing
response.text: She also asked me to thank you for the invitation. Had she not been so busy, she would have come down here herself, I'm sure of it.

response.speaker: Langqing
response.text: I hope you'll enjoy yourself here too.

response.speaker: Langqing
response.text: Indeed. See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Langqing
dialogues.text: #Hey! That final performance was really something. Did you see it too, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Have fun!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I thought there was room for improvement.

dialogues.speaker: Langqing
dialogues.text: That it does, but that's normal. I mean, even books like "How Mora is Made" aren't universally acclaimed.

dialogues.speaker: Langqing
dialogues.text: Just pick the books you enjoy reading, and listen to your favorite music.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I thought it went pretty well.

dialogues.speaker: Langqing
dialogues.text: I have to agree! I didn't think that rock 'n' roll of this kind existed, it's even different from the sort Fangfang and I heard in Fontaine. I'd love to collect some literature adjacent to the matter.

dialogues.speaker: Langqing
dialogues.text: Don't forget to drop by Wanwen Bookhouse more often if you've got the time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: One Dango Milk, please!

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: One Dango Milk, coming right up!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think it's great.

dialogues.speaker: Langqing
dialogues.text: I can tell! If you didn't like it, you wouldn't have come back just to tell me again, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: Mingxing Jewelry is well-established within the industry, though we are only taking advance orders on gems right now. We do have some other items in stock, however.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>We'd like to invite you to attend this music festival.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: A music festival, you say? Thank you. I do confess to being in the habit of collecting Radiant Spincrystals...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, then you must have music you really enjoy, right? We could play it for you — we're serious musical types!

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: Oh? Really? Well, there is this one tune... What say I hum it for you, and you play it for me in turn?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, I'll give it a go.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: Thanks for your trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How was that?

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: Ah, now that brings back memories! It reminds me of how when I was young, I would wake up very early to attend calligraphy classes at my teacher's place. It was so early that it was still dark outside, and it was terribly frightening.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: Fortunately, I would pass by the house of an old granny, and I could often hear this song drifting out from her home. It would give me a sense of peace.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: That dear old lady probably isn't with us anymore, but I've also grown, and I'm no longer as afraid of the dark, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: In any case, I've given it some serious consideration, and while I'd love to agree, it's going to be tough finding someone to watch a time-honored store like ours on such short notice.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: So let me recommend someone else to you who might attend instead — Xigu Antiques's boss, Linlang.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: She doesn't even open in the daytime, and you can either find her sleeping or wandering the streets — I reckon she'd have the free time to help.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: Regardless, thank you so much for letting me hear that song again. I hope your musical venture goes well!

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Welcome to my humble shop! We have some new items in store, if you would be so kind as to take a look at them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>We'd like to invite you to attend this music festival.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Mm? An invitation? As in, a date?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Erm, no, this is about musical exchange! By the way, do you have any songs that you like? We can play them for you — just to show you we're legit, y'know?

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: I see... Well, I do have something in mind. I'll hum, and you play. How does that sound?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, I'll give it a go.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: I'm listening.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How was that?

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: My dear guest, it would be no exaggeration to compare your performance to an adeptal hymn.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: When I was just starting in this line of work, I went to Minlin to purchase some ancient jade. On the way there, I heard music coming from Qingyun Peak.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: I was so enraptured that I wondered if it might be the music of the adepti themselves, you know? Haha. Thank you — I thought I'd never get the opportunity to hear it again.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: As for the music festival, I must say that I wouldn't call myself any kind of music enthusiast — I simply happen to like this tune. So forgive me if I must decline.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: But allow me to let slip from my lips this tidbit of gossip: I believe Mingxing Jewelry's boss, Xingxi, is a closet fan of music. Perhaps you could ask her?

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Last but not least, I wish you the best of luck with your festival.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: Found one you like? Please pay over here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>We'd like to invite you to attend this music festival.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: A music festival, you say? You know, I actually met my husband because of a song. Quite the coincidence, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Which song was it? Bet we can play it for you — we're super serious about music!

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: Oh, in that case, could you play it if I were to hum the tune?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, I'll give it a go.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: Haha, how exciting!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How was that?

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: What a wonderfully nostalgic feeling. I was immediately reminded of my studies in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: I would often go to cafes in Vasari Passage to read, and when I heard this song one day, I asked the barista what it was called.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: They didn't know, but a large fellow having some cake nearby told me that it was named "Le Souvenir avec le crepuscule." And yeah, later on, he became my husband.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: He was at the cafe meeting with his friends from a literary club back then. Ah, how nostalgic. We were all so young!

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: Oh, right! Your music festival... I fear I shan't be able to attend, but if needed, I can get my husband to go.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: He's been fiddling with some old books that haven't been selling well all day, and I haven't been able to dissuade him from doing so.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: But I'm sure such cultural exchanges would interest him. I'll ask him to bring some souvenirs along that he can give out to boot.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: Welcome. Every treasure here is unique, so we don't negotiate on the price, nor do we give refunds.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>We'd like to invite you to attend this music festival.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: A music festival? Didn't we just hold the Windblume Festival?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This one's taking place in Inazuma, Marjorie, and it's a serious musical exchange! If you've got any tunes you like, we can play it for you right here and now.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me think... Well, I don't remember this one's name, but could you play it if I were to just hum the tune?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, I'll give it a go.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: Oh, that'd be grand!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How was that?

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: This tune is so gentle, just the way I remember it.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: My dad used to play this one for me on his harmonica while we were on the way back from Springvale.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: He said that this tune represented Springvale itself, and that's where Dad's dad grew up.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: Shame that my grandfather would pass before I was ever born.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: Thanks for playing that music. You know what? I've decided that I should spend a bit more time with my dad. He's an adventurer, so he tends to spend time out in the field.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: So, if you don't mind, I might have to give this festival a pass, but if there's another opportunity, I'll come — and drag him along as well!

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Welcome to Floral Whisper. Do you need anything?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>We'd like to invite you to attend this music festival.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Is there a music event going on in the city? I'm only familiar with flowers, though, not music.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nah, this one's taking place in Inazuma. And it's totally fine if you don't know much about music, you just need to enjoy it! If there's a tune you like, we could play it for you right now, y'know?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Well... I do have something in mind. Its name escapes me, but I can hum the tune, at least. Will that do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, I'll give it a go.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Nice, woohoo!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How was that?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Ooh, you're great! This is even better than when Mr. Sayid plays it! He performed this one for us last Windblume Festival, saying that it was a traditional song from Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Donna said it sounded terrible compared to Master Diluc's playing, though.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Well, I've made up my mind. The flowers need care every day, and Inazuma's pretty far away, so I'm afraid I can't go.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Thanks for the music, though. It was lovely. On that note, I'll offer you a special price if you need flowers for your festival!

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: What'll it be today?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>We'd like to invite you to attend this music festival.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Haha, you, coming with an invitation? What's the occasion? Has Master Diluc decided to give me the day off?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, this is about a musical exchange taking place in Inazuma! If there's a song you like, we can play it for you right now.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: A song I like, you say? Hmm... I do remember Head Housemaid Adelinde hosting several small family concerts at Dawn Winery.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: They played a song at those gatherings that I do quite like. I'll do my best to hum it for you. Mind playing the song after that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, I'll give it a go.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: In that case, do excuse my amateurishness...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How was that?

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Very impressive. In fact, I should recommend to Adelinde that you be commissioned to play at the next such family event.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: As for your invitation... To be honest, I was just about ready to agree the moment you finished your performance.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: But I'm not sure if I'd want to ask Master Diluc for a day off over something this trivial — after all, he'd agree without hesitation.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: How about this, then? I'll send you a token of support for your festival. Will that do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you'll be sending us several crates of wine?

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Haha, I doubt everyone who'll be attending the festival will be of drinking age.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: As such, I'll give you some decorative banners instead. We've got them stocked in the winery warehouse — and I believe they'll come in quite handy.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Don't worry, you won't have to go fetch them yourselves. I'll have some of our traders deliver them directly.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Just consider it the "Angel's Share."

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Tsukumomono Groceries. All your wishes granted in this one place!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>We'd like to invite you to attend this music festival.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: How strange. No one's ever invited me to go attend such an event before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's why we're here! Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You must have music you really love, right, Aoi? We could play it for you — we're serious musicians!

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Music, you say? Well... There is one that I heard a long while back. I was your height when I last heard it, I believe.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: I only remember bits and pieces of it, but could you play it for me all the same?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, I'll give it a go.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How was that?

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Ah... Lovely. It seems you're quite the dab hand at making others' wishes come true.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: It's been almost twenty years since I last heard this tune. It was a boy in the neighborhood who played it for me.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: His wish was to travel and see the outside world... It's just a shame that I couldn't have been the one to help him.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Heh, well, would you look at that? I've strayed from the topic. I'm afraid I can't help with this music festival. Tsukumomono Groceries can't do without me right now.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Still, I'm glad to have heard this once more. Thank you so much.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Don't miss out on Inazuma's creative cuisine!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>We'd like to invite you to attend this music festival.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Hmm? How did you know I liked music? ... Well, to be truthful, that's where I get most of my creative ideas!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, then you must have music you really enjoy, right? We could play it for you!

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Oh, that's a long list you'd be looking at... If I had to pick one, it might be this traditional piece from Konda Village.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: That's where I started my culinary journey, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Could you play the piece if I were to hum the tune for you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, I'll give it a go.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How was that?

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Absolutely fantastic!

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: If not for the way you dress, I'd have suspected that you were from Konda Village yourself. It sounded just like the original!

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Alright, I've decided. I'm heading to this festival. Maybe immersing myself in the music there might give me some new ideas.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: I'll move my food stall over there — not that my skills are the most impressive, but I'm sure I'll add to the atmosphere at least, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Poultry skewer with BBQ sauce, salty grilled fish, kitsune ramen... Dear customer, how would you like to try some native Inazuman snacks?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>We'd like to invite you to attend this music festival.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Hmm? Did I hear you wrong? Is this a music festival or a food festival?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Music, and a serious, formal musical exchange to boot! By the way, do you have any music you enjoy? We can play it for you right now!

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Oh, you're serious, then? Well, I do have something in mind. I can try humming it for you. Could you try playing it, then?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, I'll give it a go.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Well then, this is quite the lovely surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How was that?

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Wow. What a brilliant recreation! That said, even I have no clue what this song's called, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: A fox-eared customer of ours likes humming this one when she comes over for some ramen. She's one of our VIPs. Came round a few days ago, in fact, or I wouldn't have remembered that song at all.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: ...I guess that tells you all you need to know about me and music, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: If you're looking for a food stall, I'd recommend you look for Tomoki.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: That fellow's got a right adventurous spirit. Even if he isn't a fan of music, he should be interested nonetheless.
